concerns.text: The plan claims the empirical suite will *validate* the theoretical lower‑bound scaling law (FR‑001, FR‑002, SC‑001). Validation is based on correlational evidence from synthetic experiments; this design cannot establish a causal link between variance scaling and sample‑complexity, yet the claim is presented as confirming the theory. Either re‑frame the claim as correlational or add a causal‑identification argument (e.g., controlled manipulation of variance while holding all other factors constant).

concerns.location: Implementation Phases & Task Mapping → Phase 5 – Statistical validation
concerns.text: Only four objective‑count levels (N ∈ {5,10,20,50}) are used for the regression of sample‑count vs N. With such a sparse grid the slope estimate will be highly sensitive to noise, reducing statistical power for the TOST equivalence test. Add intermediate N values (e.g., 15, 30, 40) or increase the number of runs per configuration to ensure a reliable estimate of the scaling‑law slope.

The state‑space size is fixed at 200 states for all N, but the resource guard (FR‑016) halves it only when N > 50 (which never occurs). Consequently, state‑space size varies implicitly with N only via the guard, creating a potential confound: changes in sample‑complexity could be driven by differing state‑space sizes rather than solely by N. Explicitly control for state‑space size (keep it constant across N) or include it as a covariate in the analysis.

concerns.location: Assumptions section – paragraph starting with "The synthetic multi‑objective environments generated…"
concerns.text: Construct validity relies on synthetic tabular MDPs approximating real‑world LLM reward landscapes. The current justification (random linear combinations of state features) may be insufficient to capture the non‑linear, high‑dimensional structure of actual LLM reward functions. Provide additional evidence (e.g., compare statistics of synthetic rewards to those observed in real LLM data) or broaden the synthetic generator to include non‑linear feature mappings to strengthen construct validity.
